This quiz will focus on data frame manipulation, however, you may need to rely on skills you've learned in prior weeks. 

1. load the starwars dataset from tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data(starwars)
```


2. separate the films column so that there is one film in each column (don't worry about the "c(" and ) at the end for now)
```{r}
typeof(starwars$films)
max(lengths(starwars$films))

starwars_wide <- starwars %>% 
  mutate(films = as.character(films)) %>% 
  separate(films,
           into = c("film1", "film2", "film3", "film4", "film5", "film6", "film7"),
           sep = ",",
           fill = "right"
           )
```
I used typeof() to see what the data was stored as, it returned 'list'. I used max(lengths(starwars$films)) to find out the max number of films for an individual character so I knew how many elements needed to go in 'into'. I initially tried length() which apparently returns the total for a single object. as.character() turns each list into a string which can then be used in separate().  

3. alter the data from wide data to long data
```{r}
starwars_long <- starwars_wide %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("film"),
               names_to = "film_number",
               values_to = "film",
               values_drop_na = TRUE)
```
I just used pivot_longer(), similar to what we have done in class and in the previous data manipulation assignment.

4. in the column where you stored the films, rename the levels so each film name is consistent (e.g. get rid of the "c(" and ")" )
```{r}
unique(starwars_long$film)

starwars_long <- starwars_long %>% 
  mutate(film = recode(film,
        "c(\"A New Hope\"" = "A New Hope",
        " \"The Empire Strikes Back\"" = "The Empire Strikes Back",
        " \"Return of the Jedi\"" = "Return of the Jedi",
        " \"Revenge of the Sith\"" = "Revenge of the Sith",
        " \"The Force Awakens\")" = "The Force Awakens",
        " \"The Phantom Menace\"" = "The Phantom Menace",
        " \"Attack of the Clones\"" = "Attack of the Clones",
        " \"Revenge of the Sith\")" = "Revenge of the Sith",
        "c(\"The Phantom Menace\"" = "The Phantom Menace",
        " \"The Phantom Menace\")" = "The Phantom Menace",
        " \"Return of the Jedi\")" = "Return of the Jedi",
        "c(\"The Empire Strikes Back\"" = "The Empire Strikes Back",
        " \"Attack of the Clones\")" = "Attack of the Clones",
        "The Empire Strikes Back" = "The Empire Strikes Back",
        "c(\"Return of the Jedi\"" = "Return of the Jedi",
        "c(\"Attack of the Clones\"" = "Attack of the Clones"),
        film = factor(film))

class(starwars_long$film)
```
I used unique() to get all of the possible film names, then I used recode() within mutate() to rename each in the dataset and then convert to factor.

5. Create a column in your dataset that indicates whether a character was in the first starwars film, *Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope* 
```{r}
starwars_long <- starwars_long %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  mutate(in_new_hope = any(film == "A New Hope")) %>%
  ungroup()
```
group_by(name) allows me to group the characters, since the data is long, characters appear more than once in the dataset. Then I used a logical statement to return TRUE or FALSE. Finally, I used ungroup() to prevent the code from being affected later.

6. BMI is calculated as mass in Kg/height in meters squared. You currently have mass in Kg and height in cm. Create a column that contains each character's BMI. 
```{r}
starwars_long <- starwars_long %>% 
  mutate(bmi = mass / (height / 100)^2)
```


7. create a dataframe that contains only the name, hair color, and eye color for each character. 
```{r}
starwars_mini <- starwars %>% 
  select(name, hair_color, eye_color)
```
